judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: This img is BBC's lazy-load stand-in (src grey-placeholder.png, aria-label 'image unavailable'). The real photo is its next sibling, with alt "A photo of Maricarmen Abascal at Madrid's Puerta del Sol" and a figcaption. On the live page the placeholder is only in the DOM until the real image loads, and then it is removed. Before that it is shown as a grey box. So the photo's text alternative is provided by its own img, and the placeholder's label matches what the placeholder shows. The vision crop at these bounds showed the sibling photo painted on top, which led the model to judge the placeholder against the photo. Putting a photo description on the placeholder would only repeat the sibling's alt. At most this is a best-practice note to aria-hide the placeholder, not a 1.1.1 failure for a missing alt for the photo.

judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: 'Do not share or sell my info' is the standard US privacy opt-out link. It goes to the BBC cookie settings page, where outside the UK the user turns off the personalised-advertising and other cookies. That is how the opt-out is actually carried out. The link text describes what the user goes there to do. 2.4.4 does not require link text to repeat the destination's page title, and using the title would hide the legally named purpose. Not a failure.
